python3 << 'EOF'
import numpy as np

# Data for FY 1953 to FY 1962
gold = np.array([22462.8, 21927.0, 21677.6, 21799.1, 22622.9, 21356.2, 19704.6, 19322.2, 17550.2, 16435.2])
silver = np.array([3814.3, 3863.1, 3922.4, 3994.5, 4116.6, 4306.0, 4414.1, 4394.5, 4346.5, 4317.4])

# Calculate R-squared manually
# Linear regression: silver = a + b * gold
# First, calculate means
n = len(gold)
mean_gold = np.mean(gold)
mean_silver = np.mean(silver)

# Calculate slope (b) and intercept (a)
numerator = np.sum((gold - mean_gold) * (silver - mean_silver))
denominator = np.sum((gold - mean_gold)**2)
b = numerator / denominator
a = mean_silver - b * mean_gold

# Predicted values
silver_pred = a + b * gold

# Calculate R-squared
ss_res = np.sum((silver - silver_pred)**2)
ss_tot = np.sum((silver - mean_silver)**2)
r_squared = 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)

print(f"Slope (b): {b}")
print(f"Intercept (a): {a}")
print(f"R-squared: {r_squared}")
print(f"Rounded R-squared: {round(r_squared, 2)}")
EOF

# Data for FY 1953 to FY 1962
gold = [22462.8, 21927.0, 21677.6, 21799.1, 22622.9, 21356.2, 19704.6, 19322.2, 17550.2, 16435.2]
silver = [3814.3, 3863.1, 3922.4, 3994.5, 4116.6, 4306.0, 4414.1, 4394.5, 4346.5, 4317.4]

# Calculate means
n = len(gold)
mean_gold = sum(gold) / n
mean_silver = sum(silver) / n

# Calculate standard deviations
std_gold = (sum((x - mean_gold)**2 for x in gold) / n) ** 0.5
std_silver = (sum((x - mean_silver)**2 for x in silver) / n) ** 0.5

# Calculate correlation
covariance = sum((gold[i] - mean_gold) * (silver[i] - mean_silver) for i in range(n)) / n
correlation = covariance / (std_gold * std_silver)

r_squared = correlation ** 2

print(f"Correlation: {correlation}")
print(f"R-squared (from correlation squared): {r_squared}")
print(f"R-squared (rounded): {round(r_squared, 2)}")
